Both miss every required core finding and contain material technical inaccuracies. A is slightly less misleading overall because it correctly treats Vector128.Create as accepting a span and flags a plausible fixed-size-span concern, whereas B incorrectly claims the ReadOnlySpan call is a compile-time conversion error and adds unsupported padding/uninitialized-data claims. Neither is an adequate .NET 8 review.

B follows the requested self-contained per-width dispatch and consistent vector tail implementation. A builds and is functionally correct, but violates the central dispatch requirements by conditioning the 256 guard on length and cascading to narrower dispatch for short inputs.
Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

Both preserve behavior and leave a runnable project, but B directly fulfills the throughput requirement with the available high-level vectorized framework reduction while remaining concise. A is only a narrow zero-case shortcut and adds overhead to every nonzero element, so it is materially inferior for the requested general workload.

Both miss the key legal-one-past distinction and contain incorrect safety claims. However, B supplies a correct replacement pattern satisfying the requested in-range base-plus-offset guidance, whereas A's concrete fix breaks the algorithm and safety.
Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

B is the cleaner and safer portable Vector128 solution, with a demonstrated passing run and no unjustified wider-vector specialization. Both miss the requested vectorized tail, and both otherwise provide a reasonable fallback; A's unjustified AVX2 path and error-prone unsafe implementation make B modestly preferable overall.
